findings.problem: SampleWorkflow has no enum-based typestate; lifecycle is expressed via scattered bools and a status string instead of an explicit state machine with valid transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct or mutate any combination of is_validated/is_sent/sent_at_epoch_ms simultaneously (e.g., is_sent=true with is_validated=false), producing states that no single function should ever permit.
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms with a single SampleStatus enum whose variants carry lifecycle data only on the variant that owns it (e.g., Variant::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }).

findings.problem: status field is pub String. mark_sent sets it to a bare string literal "sent". Status must be an enum, not a raw String.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can set status to any arbitrary string ("sent", "SENT", "", "pending", …), and there is no compile-time enforcement that status matches the lifecycle booleans.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with `status: SampleStatus` enum, remove mark_sent, and encode transitions in typed methods on the enum or struct.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are separate lifecycle flags. Lifecycle booleans must be typestate transitions, not independent booleans.
findings.failure_mode: The four boolean combinations (true/true, true/false, false/true, false/false) create semantically invalid states. The struct cannot enforce that is_sent implies is_validated or that sent_at_epoch_ms is Some only when is_sent is true.
findings.fix: Merge is_validated and is_sent into a single typestate enum (e.g., `enum SampleStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }`) and remove the two bool fields.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a separate optional field. Optional lifecycle data must live inside the enum variant that owns it, not as a bare Option alongside booleans.
findings.failure_mode: sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some while is_sent is false, or None while is_sent is true. The Option is decoupled from the lifecycle state, so callers cannot be forced to provide a timestamp on transition to Sent.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of the typestate enum so that the timestamp is required precisely when the workflow reaches Sent and impossible otherwise.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive carrying domain rules (uniqueness, format) but is not a newtype.
findings.failure_mode: Any function accepting or returning String can be passed a non-ID string. ID values cannot carry format rules, uniqueness invariants, or domain-specific methods at the type level.
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct WorkflowId(String)` with a smart constructor that validates the ID format, and use `WorkflowId` instead of `String` in the struct and all APIs.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String for id and status) cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: External input (deserialized JSON, CLI args, network messages) can produce a SampleWorkflow with any arbitrary id string and status string, and there is no parse-time validation or typed error to reject malformed input.
findings.fix: Add fallible smart constructors (e.g., `SampleWorkflow::parse(id: &str, …) -> Result<Self, ParseError>`) that validate and convert primitives into trusted domain values before the struct is constructed.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any performance claim
no profiler data for the hot path
no allocation analysis (mark_sent performs .to_string() allocation on every call)
no second-ring evidence tied to actual symbols or artifacts
no command evidence that any gate (cargo fmt, clippy, test) was run
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate compiles but makes illegal states representable through scattered status/String, bool lifecycle flags, and bare Option fields with no typestate enum, no smart constructor, and no parse boundary validation. Any caller can construct and mutate arbitrary invalid state combinations. Production unsafe is absent, which is positive, but the domain model has zero compile-time guarantees about valid state transitions.
